Superior canal dehiscence can mimic BPPV with sound- or pressure-induced vertigo and positional triggers, but typically includes additional features like autophony or Tullio phenomenon—absent here, lowering confidence. Vestibular migraine may present with positional dizziness but usually has associated migrainous features (e.g., headache, photophobia, aura) not reported, making it plausible but less likely. Cervicogenic dizziness is controversial and rarely causes true vertigo (spinning); it’s typically non-vertiginous unsteadiness linked to neck pathology—poorly supported by this description, hence lowest confidence."}
